answer.rationale: Competitive price pressure on SMB base requires immediate, targeted response. memory_73 confirms promotional pricing drives acquisition and revenue lift in price-sensitive SMB segments. However, this is a defensive move with inherent risk: aggressive discounting can harm unit economics and train customers toward price sensitivity, undermining long-term qualified revenue. Recommend small_guarded_test—apply promotional pricing narrowly to at-risk SMB cohorts (those in active churn conversations) rather than broad rollout. This preserves optionality: if churn stabilizes at acceptable cost, can hold; if discount erodes margins or fails to retain, can pivot to activation_messaging (memory_91: +11% engagement, +6% activation) or enterprise_sales_assist (memory_44: demo-request path outperforms on pipeline quality) as secondary levers. The other candidates (simplify_onboarding, referral_incentive, activation_messaging) are longer-cycle plays that address engagement and expansion, not acute price-driven churn. Reserved enterprise_sales_assist as a parallel or follow-on track for higher-ACV accounts where sales touch remains our strongest competitive moat. Flagged downstream risk: if promotional pricing becomes expected, future price increases will face resistance. Preserves uncertainty by limiting scope and maintaining decision points.
